item.title: ZGA joins nation in mourning Bosso executives
item.description: Brandon Moyo THE Zimbabwe Golf Association (ZGA) has joined the nation in mourning the tragic loss of Highlanders Football Club executives who died in a road traffic accident on Thursday evening. The accident, which occurred along the Harare-Bulawayo Road, claimed the lives of club chairman Colonel (Rtd) Kenneth Mhlophe, vice-chairman Sifiso “Fiso” Siziba, treasurer Nkani Khoza and club member Mbalenhle Sibanda. In a statement, the ZGA said it stood in solidarity with the Bosso family during this difficult period, adding that the three leaders’ dedication and contribution to football would always be remembered. “The Zimbabwe Golf Association extends its heartfelt condolences on the tragic passing of Mr Kenneth Mhlophe (Club Chairman), Mr Sifiso Siziba (Vice Chairman), and Mr Nkani Khoza (Treasurer). We stand with their families, loved ones, and the entire Highlanders FC community during this devastating period of bereavement. “Their immense dedication, leadership, and service to the club will forever be remembered. Our thoughts and prayers are also with the football fraternity and all those affected by this immense loss. May their dear souls rest in eternal peace,” read the statement. A joint memorial service to celebrate and honour the lives of the quartet will be held on Monday at Barbourfields Stadium. The four were granted State-assisted funerals in recognition of their service, with the memorial service expected to bring together family, friends, the football fraternity and members of the public to pay their final respects. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews
item.dc:creator: The Sunday News

item.title: Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s secure sponsorship deal with Budget Cash & Carry
item.description: Chronicle Writer THE Young Flying Stars Sports Academy (YFSSA) under-20 side has confirmed a major sponsorship agreement with Budget Cash & Carry, a leading wholesaler based in Bulawayo. The deal, signed for an undisclosed amount, will see Budget Cash & Carry supply the team’s home kit, away kit, and third kit, while also covering travel and camp logistics for the squad. [caption id=attachment_5408316 align=aligncenter width=300] Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s[/caption] This partnership represents a significant boost for the academy’s under-20 players, ensuring they are equipped with professional-standard gear and supported in their competitive development. “We are proud to partner with Young Flying Stars Sports Academy’s under-20 side, a team that embodies the future of football in Zimbabwe,” said a spokesperson for Budget Cash & Carry. [caption id=attachment_5408326 align=aligncenter width=300] Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s[/caption] “Our new partnership underlines our commitment to nurturing young talent and strengthening community sport in Bulawayo. We believe this collaboration will inspire the next generation of athletes and bring fans closer to the game.” Budget Cash & Carry has also confirmed that replica jerseys will be available for parents and fans, allowing the wider community to show their support for the under-20 side both at matches and beyond. [caption id=attachment_5408331 align=aligncenter width=300] Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s[/caption] The academy’s leadership has welcomed the sponsorship as a timely boost for the under-20 side, emphasising the importance of corporate partnerships in sustaining youth football. Director Collen Nyambiya highlighted the impact the deal will have on the players and the wider community. “This partnership with Budget Cash & Carry is a milestone for our under-20 side. Their support in providing kits and funding travel logistics ensures our young players can focus entirely on their football development. It is more than just a sponsorship; it is an investment in the future of Zimbabwean football, and we are grateful for their commitment to nurturing talent at grassroots level.” The sponsorship not only enhances the academy’s resources but also highlights the importance of corporate backing in developing Zimbabwe’s next wave of football stars. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews
item.dc:creator: The Sunday News
